summary: Sun Sep 20 13:56:02 PDT 2026 — This branch rewrites the answering prompt, empties the provisional-prompt list, and adds the voice screen, quotation verifier, cadence enforcement, and provenance refusal. It touches README prose, prompt and voice/orchestration comments and docstrings, and test prose. Ten living-text sentences are false afterwards: stale status and provisional-prompt claims, overbroad reader-facing-notice claims, an incomplete wire-record description, and two overbroad enforcement guarantees.

findings.title: Status still counts two missing endpoint capabilities
findings.sentence: Two things that endpoint does **not** yet have, both deliberate.
findings.claim: The sentence says two capabilities are still absent. After this branch, the answering prompt is an explicit avatar/provenance prompt and the answer path screens it, so the voice capability is present; only the chat screen remains absent. The rewritten ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT made the sentence false.
findings.suggestion: The endpoint now speaks as an avatar; the one thing it does **not** yet have, by design, is a chat screen.

findings.title: Status still calls the answering prompt a plain placeholder
findings.sentence:
It does not speak in Governor
Kotek's voice — the prompt it answers under is a plain placeholder, and her lexicon, pacing and
deflection framework are the next story.
findings.claim: The sentence says the answering prompt is still a plain placeholder and that this work is the next story. The branch replaces that placeholder with a finished avatar, quotation, citation, and cadence prompt; it is neither plain nor deferred to a later story.
findings.suggestion: The endpoint speaks as an avatar of Governor Kotek rather than in her own voice; its answering prompt is a finished provenance prompt, and her unsourced lexicon, pacing, and deflection framework were deliberately not adopted.

findings.title: Module docstring still calls voice prompts provisional
findings.sentence:
**Voice-bearing prompts** — the deferral the reader actually reads, and the
 * system prompt the answering model writes under — are PROVISIONAL.
findings.claim: The docstring says the reader-facing system prompt and deferral are provisional. This branch empties PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS and classifies ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT and the notices as reader-facing, finished prompts, so the present-tense claim is false.
findings.suggestion: Voice-bearing prompts are reader-facing and finished; `PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS` is empty.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes a plain placeholder prompt
findings.sentence:
The
 * placeholder below is deliberately plain, chosen at this story's approval stop
 * precisely so that nobody mistakes it for a decision about how she sounds.
findings.claim: The docstring says the prompt below is a plain placeholder that makes no voice decision. The branch replaced it with a detailed avatar-frame, quotation, citation, and cadence prompt, so both the placeholder claim and the no-voice-decision claim are false.
findings.suggestion: The answering prompt below is deliberately not an attempt at her register: it frames the avatar and requires quotations from the record.

findings.title: Stale claim that a test holds the provisional README list equal
findings.sentence:
`PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS` is the machine-readable form of that warning, and the
 * README documents the same list with a test holding the two equal — the pattern
 * the domain allowlist, the pillar list and the retrieval threshold already use.
findings.claim: The sentence claims a test holds the README and PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS equal. After the branch, PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS is empty and the README-equality test compares only the reader-facing and routing lists; no test compares a README provisional list with the empty constant.
findings.suggestion: `PROVISIONAL_PROMPTS` is the machine-readable placeholder list, now empty; the README states that it is empty, while a test holds the reader-facing and routing lists equal to the README.

findings.title: Frame comment overgeneralizes to every reader-facing notice
findings.sentence:
The frame as a reader sees it: the one wording the answer path injects and every
 * reader-facing notice opens with.
findings.claim: The comment says every reader-facing notice opens with DISPLAY_FRAME. FAILURE_NOTICE is in READER_FACING_PROMPTS and deliberately begins with “Something went wrong…” rather than the avatar frame, so the universal claim is false.
findings.suggestion: The frame as a reader sees it: the one wording the answer path injects and the avatar-voiced notices open with.

findings.title: Reader-facing list comment includes a deliberately neutral notice
findings.sentence:
The prompts a reader actually meets — the avatar's own voice, finished rather
 * than provisional.
findings.claim: The comment characterizes all prompts in this list as the avatar's own voice. The list includes FAILURE_NOTICE, whose own docstring says it is deliberately not in character and whose text is neutral infrastructure prose.
findings.suggestion: The prompts a reader actually meets; the avatar-voiced ones are finished, while `FAILURE_NOTICE` is deliberately neutral.

findings.title: Wire documentation omits provenance text in streamed tokens
findings.sentence: | `streamed_tokens` | Text for the reader — either the generated answer, or the fixed deferral |
findings.claim: The README says streamed_tokens carries only generated answer text or the fixed deferral. The new refusal path emits PROVENANCE_NOTICE as a streamed_tokens record, so the exhaustive either/or description is false.
findings.suggestion: | `streamed_tokens` | Text for the reader — generated answer text, the fixed deferral, or the provenance notice |

findings.title: Prompt overstates quotation-like mark enforcement
findings.sentence: An answer containing one is stopped.
findings.claim: The prompt says an answer containing any other quotation-like mark is stopped. The lexer treats everything between the outer curly quotation marks as quotation content and emits it as a quotation, so a faithful quotation containing a guillemet, low quote, backtick, or similar mark is not stopped.
findings.suggestion: An answer using one outside a quotation is stopped; inside a quotation it is the record's own content.

findings.title: Provenance documentation omits the no-citation release path
findings.sentence:
An unverifiable quotation, a quotation in the wrong marks, or an opening that speaks as the Governor
and cannot be repaired stops the answer with a **provenance notice** — never the infrastructure
failure notice.
findings.claim: The README says an unverifiable quotation stops the answer. The streaming path explicitly excludes the verifier's no-citation result from refusal, logs it, and then emits the quotation, so a quotation returned as UnverifiedQuotation with reason no-citation can reach the reader without a provenance notice.
findings.suggestion: A fabricated or misattributed quotation, a quotation in the wrong marks, or an opening that speaks as the Governor and cannot be repaired stops the answer with a provenance notice; a verbatim quotation with no recognised citation is logged and released.
